before.name: Reservoirs, script, metals and pottery used in the city of Dholavira in Indus Valley Civilization

after.name: c. 2650 BC: Dholavira Stage I in one chronology; dating debated

r2SourceEvidence.review_note: One scheme places Dholavira Stage I c.2650–2550 BCE, but newer proposals and UNESCO place initial occupation earlier, with phase definitions differing. This one-year -2650 slot is a reference to that scheme, not a confirmed founding or a dated event. UNESCO describes site-wide reservoirs, script-related finds, materials and infrastructure but does not date each to 2650; the former entry implied all existed in that year and had an unjustified political effect. The earlier r2_dholavira_early_c3000 contextual record represents another chronology and overlaps this reference. 20 km radius is a game setting.

r2SourceEvidence.review_note: The overview gives c.2750–2600 for ED II, while another bullet says a boundary c.2650 and the detailed ED article provides multiple alternative schemes or omits ED II altogether. This is one approximate periodization, not a definite yearly event, and overlaps the previously retained ED I and boundary notes because the schemes disagree. Point and 250 km radius are regional game references, not territorial limits. NewsIndex may repeat this note annually.

before.name: A bronze bar produced in Nippur (Sumeria) defines the cubit

after.name: c. 2650 BC: Nippur copper-alloy measuring rod; dating and function uncertain

r2SourceEvidence.review_note: The century overview dates a Nippur rod to c.2650, not 2700. The Cubit and Measuring rod articles describe a copper-alloy bar and attribute the measuring-standard interpretation to Eckhard Unger; measurement length and archaeological date are approximate. Unger biography says he identified it in the museum, while the Cubit article says he found it while excavating: discovery circumstances conflict. The -2650 slot is a dating reference, not exact manufacture, discovery, earliest claim, or proof that this object invented a universal cubit. Coordinate is Nippur area, 20 km a game radius; museum is in Istanbul.
